paper_title: SPARC: Geometry-Guided Attention Pruning for Long-Horizon Camera-Controlled Video Generation

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: We present SPARC, a geometry-guided attention pruning framework that turns the native self-attention of pretrained video diffusion transformers into a unified mechanism for camera control and persistent scene memory. Our key insight is that attention connectivity can simultaneously serve as geometric conditioning for camera control and spatial addressing for historical memory retrieval. Motivated by the asymmetric contextual requirements of reconstructing observed content and synthesizing novel regions, SPARC restricts observed tokens to geometrically corresponding historical tokens and local spatiotemporal context, while preserving dense attention for unobserved regions. Correspondence-aware attention biasing and order-invariant historical positioning further enable stable retrieval across long temporal gaps. Without introducing additional learnable control or memory modules, SPARC achieves precise camera adherence and faithful scene revisitation while substantially reducing attention computation. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of aggressive attention pruning in improving camera adherence, revisit consistency, and visual fidelity, with an inference speedup of over 50x when combined with four-step distillation. Project page is available at https://zju3dv.github.io/SPARC.

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: 1. Introduction We present SPARC, geometry-guided attention pruning framework that turns the native self-attention of pretrained video diffusion transformers into unified mechanism for camera control and persistent scene memory. Our key insight is that attention connectivity can simultaneously serve as geometric conditioning for camera control and spatial addressing for historical memory retrieval. Motivated by the asymmetric contextual requirements of reconstructing observed content and synthesizing novel regions, SPARC restricts observed tokens to geometrically corresponding historical tokens and local spatiotemporal context, while preserving dense attention for unobserved regions. Correspondenceaware attention biasing and order-invariant historical positioning further enable stable retrieval across long temporal gaps. Without introducing additional learnable control or memory modules, SPARC achieves precise camera adherence and faithful scene revisitation while substantially reducing attention computation. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of aggressive attention pruning in improving camera adherence, revisit consistency, and visual fidelity, with an inference speedup of over 50 when combined with four-step distillation. Project page is available at https://zju3dv.github.io/SPARC. Project Lead. Corresponding Author. Recent advances in video diffusion transformers [1, 11, 17, 28, 34, 35] have enabled increasingly realistic and temporally coherent video generation, bringing interactive world generation closer to reality [2, 6, 10, 29, 55]. However, long-horizon generation under prescribed camera trajectories remains challenging. Beyond synthesizing plausible frames, model must accurately follow camera movements and preserve scene identity when returning to previously visited locations. Existing approaches primarily rely on camera-conditioning modules [3, 12, 22, 52], explicit 3D reconstruction [30, 42, 46, 51, 57], or historical frames as context [13, 32, 33, 43, 50] to support controllable long-horizon generation. While effective, these mechanisms introduce additional architectural complexity or rely on computationally expensive dense attention over historical observations. Rather than adding dedicated control or memory modules, we explore an alternative perspective: can attention connectivity itself serve as unified mechanism for camera control and persistent scene memory in pretrained video diffusion transformers? Both capabilities require spatially grounded access to historical visual evidence, yet conventional dense attention allows unrestricted interactions with historical tokens, without explicitly enforcing spatial correspondence. Such interactions introduce computational redundancy and may interfere with accurate historical retrieval. 1 relative to the original backbone. Our main contributions are summarized as follows: We reveal that camera control and persistent memory share common requirement for spatially grounded historical retrieval, motivating unified attention-based solution. We propose SPARC, geometry-guided asymmetric attention pruning framework that uses native self-attention for camera conditioning and persistent memory retrieval, without additional learnable control or memory modules. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SPARC achieves superior camera adherence, revisit consistency, and visual fidelity, while substantially reducing attention computation and inference latency for minute-long video generation. 2. Related Work Camera Control in Video Generation. Recent works incorporate camera trajectories into video generation for controllable viewpoint changes. Some encode camera poses or Plucker rays as conditioning embeddings [3, 12, 43, 58], or modify attention mechanisms to incorporate camera geometry [22, 47, 52]. Others leverage explicit 3D priors to provide pixel-aligned geometric guidance through projection [5, 15, 26, 30, 44, 45, 51]. These approaches often introduce additional conditioning mechanisms or geometric representations, increasing architectural complexity and computational overhead. Long-Horizon Memory in Video Generation. Longhorizon generation requires efficient history management to mitigate the quadratic complexity of growing attention contexts. Existing methods reconstruct explicit 3D memories for target-view projection [7, 19, 40, 42, 56, 57], retrieve relevant keyframes based on camera frustum overlap [21, 33, 43, 50], or compress historical context at the cost of potential information loss [13, 20, 27, 32, 41, 53]. However, these methods often incur additional memory management overhead or redundant attention computation. In contrast, SPARC directly prunes the backbones native selfattention to retrieve geometrically relevant historical evidence, enabling precise camera control and persistent scene memory without additional learnable modules. 3. Methods 3.1. Problem Formulation and Preliminaries Camera-Conditioned Autoregressive Video Generation. Given an initial image I1, text prompt y, and prescribed camera trajectory {ct}T t=1, our goal is to autoregressively generate long-horizon video with precise camera control and persistent scene consistency. Following [50], we maintain streaming history bank Bt = {(Is, zs, cs, Ds)}s<t, containing previously generated frames, their VAE latents, camera poses, and estimated depth maps. For each upcoming camera chunk ct+1:t+k, we retrieve compact set of Figure 2. Redundancy of dense full self-attention. Most target regions have been observed in historical frames and require only sparse geometric correspondences for faithful reconstruction, while newly revealed regions benefit from broader contextual interactions. Our key insight is that attention pruning can serve as geometric conditioning and memory addressing, rather than merely computational optimization. Given target camera pose, geometric correspondences determine which historical tokens each target token can access. Crucially, observed regions attend to geometrically matched historical evidence and local context, while unseen regions retain broader attention for plausible synthesis. As shown in Fig. 2, most target regions require only sparse historical correspondences, enabling efficient information routing that supports both camera control and persistent memory retrieval. Building upon this insight, we introduce SPARC, geometry-guided attention pruning framework that directly restructures the native self-attention of pretrained video diffusion transformers. SPARC constructs token-level historical correspondences through local geometric projection and applies asymmetric attention routing based on target-region visibility. Observed tokens access geometrically matched historical evidence and local temporal context, whereas unobserved tokens retain dense attention for flexible content synthesis. Correspondence-aware attention biasing further strengthens historical evidence against the substantially larger local context, while order-invariant positioning eliminates artificial temporal ordering biases among retrieved historical observations. Without introducing additional learnable control or memory modules, SPARC exploits the pretrained models inherent capabilities through lightweight self-attention adaptation, enabling camera control and persistent scene consistency. We train SPARC on DL3DV-10K [24], largescale real-world dataset with diverse camera trajectories. Each sequence is divided into 145-frame clips at resolution of 480 832. We employ VGGT-Omega [38] to estimate camera poses and per-frame depths, and generate video captions with Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct [4]. We construct training samples under two conditioning modes. In image-to-video (I2V) mode, we train on the first 73 frames, with the initial frame providing geometric references for target-view correspondences. In history-to-video (H2V) mode, the first 73 frames constitute the history bank, from which 4 keyframes are retrieved following the coveragebased strategy in Sec. 3.4 to establish token correspondence cache; the remaining 72 frames serve as generation targets. Implementation Details. We adopt Wan2.1-I2V-14B [35] as our pretrained backbone and implement the pruned sparse attention masks using FlexAttention [8]. We first perform self-attention fine-tuning with our pruning strategy for 3K iterations, followed by DMD2 distillation [48] into fourstep student using rank-32 LoRA adapters [14] with CFG scale of 5 for an additional 2K iterations. Both stages are optimized using AdamW on 32 GPUs (96 GB each), with learning rate of 1 105. 4.2. Quantitative Evaluation Baselines and Metrics. We compare SPARC against recent memory-augmented camera-controlled video generation methods, including explicit-3D approaches Lyra2 [32], Spatia [57], HY-WorldStereo [56], and UCM [45], as well as implicit approaches HY-WorldPlay [33], LingbotWorld [31], and Infinite-World [41]. We first evaluate all methods on DL3DV-Evaluation [24]. Given only the same initial frame, each method autoregressively generates subsequent frames along the ground-truth camera trajectory. We evaluate visual fidelity and temporal quality using SSIM [39], LPIPS [54], and FVD [37]. To assess camera-control accuracy, we estimate camera trajectories from generated videos using ViPE [16], align them with ground truth via Umeyama alignment [36], and report TransErr, RotErr, and Absolute Trajectory Error (ATE). We further evaluate long-horizon revisitation on 50 randomly sampled scenes from the WorldScore Static set [9] using closed-loop camera trajectories. We report Content Alignment, Subjective Quality, Style Consistency, and Photometric Consistency, together with Revisit SSIM and Revisit LPIPS, which measure the fidelity of recovered scene content against reference observations at matched camera poses. Quantitative and Qualitative Comparison. As shown in Tab. 1, SPARC performs favorably across the evaluated metrics and benchmarks. Our method reduces ATE by 54% compared with the strongest baseline, demonstrating improved trajectory adherence, as further illustrated in Fig. 5. SPARC also achieves superior content alignment, subjective quality, and revisit performance on WorldScore, demonstrating its ability to faithfully recover observed content after long temporal gaps without compromising generation quality. The qualitative comparisons in Figs. 4 and 6 further demonstrate the advantages of SPARC over existing methods. Lyra2 delivers competitive visual fidelity but gradually drifts from the target camera path under extended camera motion. Spatia and HY-WorldStereo exhibit progressive scene distortion and visual degradation, consistent with their susceptibility to accumulated reconstruction errors in explicit 3D memory. UCM initially preserves coherent appearance but gradually deviates from the observed scene over extended rollouts. Among implicit methods, HY-WorldPlay and Lingbot-World struggle with both accurate camera control and revisitation, whereas Infinite-World maintains comparatively stable appearance but insufficiently follows the prescribed trajectory precisely. In contrast, SPARC maintains coherent appearance and accurate camera control throughout the rollout, despite introducing the lightest architectural modification to the original DiT architecture among all compared methods. 6 Figure 6. Qualitative comparison of revisitation on WorldScore-Static. Each scene follows closed-loop camera trajectory (top view), and frames are sampled along the roaming time. Baselines either distort the scene or fail to recover the originally observed content upon revisiting, whereas our SPARC faithfully restores the scene at both revisits. See Supp. for additional scenes and video comparisons. Table 2. Ablation on attention pruning. Geometric correspondence attention, local window attention, and correspondence bias provide complementary improvements in reconstruction fidelity, while shared historical RoPE further enhances generation quality. Ablation Study To investigate the contributions of individual design choices to generation quality and computational efficiency, we conduct controlled novel-view generation experiments on Tanks and Temples Dataset [18]. We sample camera-calibrated multi-view images as historical observations and generate 7 videos along held-out camera trajectories with ground-truth frames available for evaluation. All variants are trained with identical data and optimization settings following Sec. 4.1. Attention Pruning Components. We first establish baseline that retains the pretrained DiTs dense self-attention and incorporates camera conditioning through the camera adapter following [12]. Despite producing relative viewpoint changes, it exhibits poor camera adherence and progressive visual degradation, yielding the lowest fidelity in Tab. 2 and Fig. 7. As illustrated in Fig. 8, its historical attention peaks frequently deviate from geometrically corresponding regions, with only 0.41.3% of the historical attention mass assigned to matched regions for the illustrated queries. Introducing correspondence bias into dense attention substantially improves camera adherence and reconstruction fidelity  (Fig. 7)  , revealing that accurate camera control can emerge from sparse subset of spatially aligned attention interactions. However, its inferior performance to our pruned counterpart suggests that prioritizing relevant interactions alone cannot fully eliminate interference from unrelated tokens. We then progressively examine our pruning strategy. Restricting observed target queries only to geometrically corresponding historical tokens (Nhist) enables camera-guided generation and memory retrieval directly through attention pruning, but produces mosaic-like artifacts due to insufficient local context. These findings demonstrate that geometry-guided pruning does more than reduce computation: it restructures information flow to suppress irrelevant interactions and strengthen spatially aligned historical evidence, providing unified mechanism for camera control and persistent scene memory. Order-Invariant Historical Positioning. Since coveragebased retrieval selects keyframes by geometric relevance, their concatenation order carries no meaningful temporal information in long-horizon rollouts, and the generation should therefore be invariant to it. To verify this, we run inference under four permutations of the retrieved history, and evaluate our shared historical RoPE against conventional sequential RoPE. Permuting the retrieved historical frames introduces substantial appearance variations under sequential RoPE, whereas our shared indexing produces nearly identical outputs, as illustrated in Fig. 7 and Tab. 3. This highlights the importance of eliminating spurious positional biases toward temporally adjacent historical frames to enable permutationFigure 8. Attention weight visualization. Given target queries, dense attention with the camera adapter exhibits attention peaks that deviate from geometrically corresponding historical regions. invariant memory retrieval. Computational Analysis. We profile the computational cost of each design in Tab. 4. Each variant generates 72-frame chunk at 480 832 conditioned on 9 historical latents, i.e., 42,120 tokens in total, of which 99.0% of target tokens are observed. All measurements are conducted on single 96 GB GPU. Restricting observed queries to historical correspondences skips 98.1% of querykey pairs, reducing attention FLOPs by 53 and per-step latency by 2.70. Adding local window attention with = 2 enlarges this scope but still skips 86.7% of querykey pairs. Distilling the pruned model into 4-step student removes classifier-free guidance and reduces function evaluations from 100 to 4, achieving 53.6 speedup in per-chunk DiT inference. Training-Free Dynamic Scene Generation. Although trained exclusively on static scenes, SPARC naturally extends to dynamic scene generation without additional training. Since geometric correspondences govern the scope of historical attention, manipulating these correspondences enables controllable object motion while preserving background consistency. Specifically, as shown in Fig. 10, we segment the foreground object and shift its correspondence locations along prescribed motion trajectory, allowing SPARC to synthesize natural object motion consistent with the specified trajectory. These results highlight the potential of correspondence manipulation for joint camera and object motion control in training-free manner. Figure 9. Additional long-horizon generation results. Without any degradation-aware augmentation, SPARC generates high-fidelity, minute-long videos with precise camera adherence and persistent scene consistency. Table 4. Computational efficiency. By combining attention pruning with 4-step distillation, SPARC achieves 50 inference speedup over the original dense backbone.

Conclusion We present SPARC, geometry-guided attention pruning framework that unifies camera control and persistent scene memory by restructuring the native self-attention of pretrained video diffusion transformers. Our key insight is that attention connectivity itself can serve as geometric conditioning, and that selectively removing geometrically irrelevant interactions improves spatial control, revisit consistency, and computational efficiency. Without additional learnable control or memory modules, SPARC enables efficient minutelong camera-controlled video generation. Our findings highlights attention connectivity as promising interface for unlocking the inherent spatial reasoning and memory capabilities of pretrained video diffusion models. Limitations. SPARC relies on external geometry estimation to establish spatial correspondences, introducing additional computational overhead. promising direction is to jointly learn geometry reasoning and attention connectivity within the generative model, enabling more unified and efficient framework.
